title: Mathematics — notable papers from the 2026-11-09 arXiv announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart. Ordering is inferred from stated results, cross-subfield relevance, and artifacts; attention/citation evidence is sparse for these new papers, so the list is notable recent papers rather than a measured popularity ranking.

sections.title: The Woo-Yong conjecture
sections.abstract: The author proves the Woo-Yong conjecture for type A Schubert varieties, extends divisor-class detection to torsion classes in arbitrary finite crystallographic type, and gives a type D example showing why the broader claim needs qualification.
sections.claimed_result: For every scheme point of a type A complete or partial flag Schubert variety, local divisor classes are detected at the generic points of the maximal singular components through that point; applying this to the canonical divisor proves the Woo-Yong conjecture.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Full local detection is proved for type A Schubert varieties. For arbitrary finite crystallographic type, injectivity is proved only on the torsion subgroup of the source local class group.
sections.unique_caveat: A type D family shows that the unrestricted analogue fails outside type A; the torsion qualification is essential.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Named conjecture resolution, stronger all-Weil-divisor statement in type A, extension to finite-type torsion classes, and ancillary verification programs and exact certificates on the arXiv record.

sections.title: The small ball problem for the Brownian sheet: sharp bounds via entropy numbers in L-infinity
sections.abstract: The authors settle the uniform small-deviation conjecture for Brownian sheets in every dimension d >= 2 using sharp entropy and Kolmogorov estimates, and derive related bounds for mixed-smoothness classes and Gaussian fields.
sections.claimed_result: For the d-dimensional Brownian sheet, -log P(||B||_infinity <= epsilon) is comparable to epsilon^(-2)(log(1/epsilon))^(2d-1) as epsilon tends to zero, for d >= 2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: B is the centered continuous Gaussian sheet on [0,1]^d with covariance product_i min(s_i,t_i), measured in the uniform norm; d >= 2.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem gives asymptotic order with dimension-dependent constants, not a leading constant; the separate deterministic Haar-function small-ball inequality remains open.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Theorem 1.1 resolves the stated conjecture in every dimension d >= 2; the result links probability and functional analysis, and the abstract links a Lean certificate.

sections.title: The BCC lattice is the optimal 3D lattice quantizer for all p >= 1
sections.abstract: The author proves that among three-dimensional lattices of covolume one, the body-centered cubic lattice uniquely minimizes every finite p-th moment of the Voronoi cell, up to orthogonal transformations, resolving the Graf-Luschgy conjecture for lattice quantizers.
sections.claimed_result: For every 1 <= p < infinity, the unit-covolume BCC lattice uniquely minimizes the normalized Voronoi p-moment among full-rank 3D lattices, modulo orthogonal transformations.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The optimization is over Bravais lattices in R^3 with covolume one; p is finite and at least one.
sections.unique_caveat: The result concerns lattice quantizers, not unrestricted point configurations; the proof includes computer-assisted interval/polynomial bounds not independently checked here.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Theorem 1.1 gives a unique optimizer over the full finite p range, resolves a named conjecture, spans four mathematical classifications, and describes exact interval/polynomial comparisons.

sections.title: Macdonald intersections and the N!/k conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors prove the conjectured Frobenius-characteristic formula for intersections of Garsia-Haiman modules and, as a consequence, resolve the N!/k conjecture using Hilbert-scheme geometry.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove the Bergeron-Garsia-predicted Frobenius characteristic formula for the relevant module intersections; Corollary 1.1 gives dimension N!/k under the same hypotheses.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: For n >= 2, k >= 1, N=n-1, and a partition lambda of n, take k distinct partitions of N obtained by removing a corner cell from lambda; the formula concerns the intersection of their associated bigraded Garsia-Haiman modules.
sections.unique_caveat: The result applies to this corner-removal family of module intersections and does not resolve other Macdonald-polynomial conjectures.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A named conjecture is resolved, bridging algebraic combinatorics and algebraic geometry; the arXiv abstract identifies Hilbert-scheme geometry as the proof framework.

sections.title: Harper's beyond square-root conjecture for random matrices
sections.abstract: For a Haar unitary matrix U_N, the authors prove E|tr(Sym^k U_N)| tends to zero as min(N,k) tends to infinity, settling the random-matrix version of Harper's conjecture without restricting k/N.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish the vanishing first absolute moment for traces of symmetric powers of Haar unitary matrices as min(N,k) tends to infinity, using exact weighted trace moments and a Gaussian change of measure.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: U_N is Haar-distributed on the unitary group of size N; both N and k tend to infinity, with no condition on their ratio.
sections.unique_caveat: This proves the random-matrix analogue, not Harper's original arithmetic conjecture about random multiplicative functions or its number-theoretic consequences.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The paper settles a specifically named random-matrix conjecture uniformly across relative-growth regimes and connects number theory, probability, and holomorphic multiplicative chaos.

sections.title: Sharp universality thresholds for random profinite groups
sections.abstract: The authors determine sharp conditions for random quotients of free profinite groups to converge to the Liu-Wood distribution, including a sharp factor-count threshold and an exact parity-and-length criterion for random words.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed u >= 0 and quotients of the free profinite group on n generators by n+u independent random relations, the authors prove universality under stated coset-balance conditions; for fixed-length random words, convergence holds exactly when lengths are eventually odd and ell_n-log n tends to infinity.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The number u is fixed; relations are independent, and the factor-product results require the paper's coset-balance hypotheses. The word-length threshold is asymptotic in n.
sections.unique_caveat: The thresholds are model-specific and are not claimed for arbitrary dependent relations or every random profinite-group construction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract supplies sufficient and sharp failure thresholds plus an if-and-only-if criterion; probability and group theory are both central classifications.

sections.title: The maximum size of 3-distance binary codes
sections.abstract: For every n >= 24, the largest family in {-1,1}^n with at most three distinct pairwise Hamming distances has size binomial(n,3)+n, and the threshold n=24 is best possible.
sections.claimed_result: Every binary family whose pairwise Hamming distances take at most three distinct values has size at most binomial(n,3)+n for n >= 24, and a family attaining the bound is exhibited.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The ambient space is {-1,1}^n with Hamming distance; 3-distance means at most three distinct distances among pairs of distinct vectors.
sections.unique_caveat: The classification of extremal families remains unresolved; at n=24 there is a non-isometric extremal construction.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: An exact extremal value holds uniformly for n >= 24; the threshold is sharp by the length-23 dual binary Golay code, and the theorem covers all choices of the three distances.

sections.title: Division ring extensions and a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture
sections.abstract: The authors construct division-ring extensions yielding, in characteristic zero, a hereditary right pure-semisimple ring of infinite representation type, a counterexample to the pure semisimplicity conjecture; for p >= 3 they construct finite-type examples.
sections.claimed_result: In characteristic zero, the authors claim a hereditary right pure-semisimple ring with infinitely many indecomposable finitely generated modules; for every prime p >= 3, they construct a hereditary artinian ring of finite representation type with Coxeter diagram I_2(p+2).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The counterexample is built from a division-ring extension over a characteristic-zero field; the second family is for fields of characteristic p >= 3.
sections.unique_caveat: The counterexample is one-sided (right pure semisimplicity); it does not assert left pure semisimplicity or a two-sided analogue.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: An explicit counterexample to a named conjecture and a family of characteristic-p constructions connect ring theory and representation theory.

sections.title: Sharper energy scaling bounds of the singularly perturbed Tartar square
sections.abstract: The author improves the lower-bound argument so that the lower and upper bounds for the singularly perturbed Tartar square have matching logarithmic powers, with order exp(-C sqrt(log(epsilon^-1))) for suitable constants.
sections.claimed_result: The author claims matching logarithmic exponents in the energy scaling law, improving the ansatz-free lower bound and sharpening an upper construction by iterated branching.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The setting is the singular perturbation parameter epsilon for the Tartar-square problem; the result is an asymptotic scaling estimate with suitable lower- and upper-bound constants.
sections.unique_caveat: Matching exponents do not identify a common sharp constant; the paper quantifies a remaining gap between lower- and upper-bound constants.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It closes a previously reported logarithmic-power mismatch using refined Fourier multipliers for the lower bound and iterated branching for the upper bound.

sections.title: Tensor value and the 9/4 bound for matrix multiplication
sections.abstract: The authors give an exposition of the recent matrix-multiplication exponent bound 9/4 over every field, using a fractional symmetrized tensor value and a superadditivity inequality for partially direct sums.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove a superadditivity inequality for a power of their fractional symmetrized tensor value; with polynomial-multiplication tensor degenerations from the prior OpenAI proof, this yields the stated 9/4 bound.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The bound is stated over every field; the method concerns tensor degenerations and partially direct sums with a shared factor and independent subspaces in the other factors.
sections.unique_caveat: This preprint is an exposition and alternate proof framework for a result already announced by OpenAI, not the original discovery of the 9/4 bound.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: It is cross-listed in representation theory and computational complexity and supplies a tensor-value framework for deriving a major recent exponent bound; the abstract calls the work an exposition.
